article.title: How Discord Stores Trillions of Messages
article.author: Bo Ingram
article.access: Public article accessible through web extraction; a direct urllib HTML request returned HTTP 403
article.read_scope: Complete accessible main narrative from Cassandra Troubles through Several Months Later, including migration and operational outcome; embedded schema/diagram/graph images not independently inspected; linked earlier articles not counted
article.fact_summary: Hot partitions caused cascading latency. Discord added intermediary data services that coalesced overlapping reads and routed channels consistently. Its checkpointed migration stalled on tombstone-heavy ranges; selected reads were compared before cutover. These observations motivate bounded-load and migration-evidence checks, not a portable throughput promise.
article.limits: Historical company account. It does not specify a complete admission algorithm, cross-user authorization/freshness policy, dual-write reconciliation protocol or universal storage durability guarantee.

practices.provenance: Engineering inference from the article's failure mechanism, current diagnostic and runtime contracts; not a claim of Discord's unpublished implementation
practices.trigger: One tenant/key/partition drives tail latency or origin saturation while aggregate capacity appears adequate.
practices.failure: Concentrated concurrent work consumes shared resources; added callers or frontend replicas amplify the same constrained origin.
practices.mechanism: Measure request concentration separately from stored size; choose per-key admission/coalescing plus an aggregate origin bound and explicit bounded waiting/rejection.
practices.conditions: The constrained resource and routing scope are known; callers may share equivalent reads or accept the selected bounded overload response.
practices.limits: Affinity does not spread one hot key. Process-local control is not a global bound; routing changes can create multiple active owners. Unique-key load may offer no coalescing benefit.
practices.counterexample: A semaphore limits active queries but an unlimited number of waiting tasks or tracked keys exhausts memory.
practices.verification: Mix one hot key, many unique keys and cold traffic; bound active work, waiters and key cardinality, then cancel/error/remap owners and observe release and unaffected work.
practices.overlap: Hot-key behavior and bulkheads already exist; concrete coalescer scope, waiter cardinality and skew-isolation checks are the gap.

practices.provenance: Proposed correctness analysis supported by the local Group/key API; not a reported Discord bug
practices.trigger: Concurrent callers join shared reads with differing visibility, query arguments, consistency requirements or deadlines.
practices.failure: A waiter receives another caller's unauthorized or too-old result; cancellation of one caller unintentionally aborts shared work, or detached waiters leak resources.
practices.mechanism: Define result equivalence and scope every result-changing input, or check authorization/freshness per waiter. Own the shared operation's deadline/cancellation separately from waiter detachment.
practices.conditions: The read contract and result-sharing scope are explicit; freshness is verified by an actual source/version protocol.
practices.limits: Singleflight is neither a cache nor a freshness guarantee. Forgetting a key can admit a second operation before the old one finishes. Coalescing mutations needs a separate durable effect protocol.
practices.counterexample: A read starts before revision 8 commits; a post-commit read requiring revision 8 joins it and receives revision 7.
practices.verification: Force that history and cross-tenant/visibility mismatch; cancel the first then all waiters, fail the origin and verify bounded cleanup under the chosen policy.
practices.overlap: Existing concurrency-correctness delayed-fill/version rules remain authoritative. The accepted placement keeps shared in-flight read equivalence and the dependent-reader history in capacity; cache-coherence.md was not changed.

practices.provenance: Engineering validation proposal; the article's samples are not treated as proof of every historical record
practices.trigger: Bulk storage copy approaches completion, especially with cold ranges, deletions, TTLs or writes continuing during migration.
practices.failure: Aggregate progress or popular sampled reads hide missing cold data, incomplete ranges, changed expiry, or incorrect last-write ordering.
practices.mechanism: Track every required range and unresolved failure; define the comparison boundary and reconciliation path; compare payload and relevant delete/TTL/write-time semantics with explicit tolerances.
practices.conditions: The selected engine and migrator expose sufficient source positions, range identity and comparison evidence.
practices.limits: A live scan is not automatically one snapshot. Row counts and absence of sampled mismatches have limited coverage; preserve existing dual-write and cutover recovery rules.
practices.counterexample: A cold range times out while all popular sampled records match, or copying a row resets its remaining TTL.
practices.verification: Inject a failed range, missing payload, deletion, changed TTL/write timestamp and concurrent update; block completion until coverage and semantic comparison meet the declared contract.
practices.overlap: Compatibility and business comparison already exist. microservice-extraction/data-transition.md already handles dual-write ambiguity and row-count insufficiency; avoid duplicating its ownership workflow.

practices.provenance: Current primary storage-document constraint, not adoption of Discord's maintenance action
practices.trigger: Deletion-heavy ranges or compaction backlog cause timeouts during ordinary reads or migration.
practices.failure: An operator trades deletion safety for lower tombstone pressure or mistakes incomplete diagnostic coverage for clean data.
practices.mechanism: Inspect deployed engine/version, repair/outage history, deletion retention and compaction resource budget before choosing maintenance.
practices.conditions: Applies only where the storage engine uses the relevant tombstone and repair mechanism.
practices.limits: Cassandra settings are not portable ScyllaDB defaults; an empty large-partition diagnostic is not an exhaustive absence proof.
practices.counterexample: A replica misses a delete, retention is shortened, and the old value returns after rejoin.
practices.verification: In an authorized disposable cluster, test delete/TTL across missed replication, repair and compaction, then verify continued absence.
practices.overlap: Prefer a conditional caveat/source link alongside migration validation, not a new maintenance skill or automatic command.

runtime_sources.title: singleflight package
runtime_sources.version: golang.org/x/sync v0.23.0; observed documentation version, not asserted to be latest
runtime_sources.read_scope: Group, Do, DoChan, Forget and Result contracts
runtime_sources.findings: Duplicate suppression uses a Group and key; concurrent callers share returned result/error. DoChan's result channel is not closed. Forget allows a future call to run without waiting for an earlier one.

runtime_sources.title: singleflight.go
runtime_sources.read_scope: Group map/mutex, Do and DoChan registration/waiting, doCall completion, Forget removal
runtime_sources.findings: State and duplicate tracking are local to a Group. The interface has no context argument; caller cancellation policy is not supplied. The primitive does not bound distinct keys or all waiting callers.

runtime_sources.title: tokio::sync::Semaphore
runtime_sources.publisher: Tokio project documentation hosted on docs.rs
runtime_sources.version: 1.53.1 displayed by latest page on access
runtime_sources.read_scope: Overview/fairness, incoming/outgoing concurrency examples, acquisition/cancellation and try_acquire contracts
runtime_sources.findings: Permits bound simultaneous holders, with acquisition placement determining whether task creation is bounded. Fair multi-permit acquisition can delay smaller requests; cancelling acquisition loses queue position. Application policy still owns total waiting population.

runtime_sources.title: ScyllaDB Large Partitions Table
runtime_sources.read_scope: Detection scope, node-local results, metadata-backed virtual tables, feature activation and upgrade limits
runtime_sources.findings: Measurements are per SSTable partition fragment and node. New virtual tables use bounded metadata written into SSTables; older SSTables may have no records. Empty diagnostics cannot prove absence of large logical partitions or hot request traffic.

runtime_sources.title: Tombstones
runtime_sources.read_scope: Deletion markers, unavailable replicas, grace, compaction eligibility and repaired-data gating
runtime_sources.findings: Expiry alone does not remove deletion evidence; compaction must account for shadowed older data. Replicas missing deletion can resurrect data after evidence disappears. Apply the deployed engine's repair/retention contract before changing maintenance.

runtime_sources.title: Validate the Migration
runtime_sources.read_scope: Validator semantics, comparison configuration, deployment modes; commands read but not executed
runtime_sources.findings: Supports TTL and write-time comparisons with explicit tolerances. The instruction to pause writes on both sides is specifically for MySQL-to-ScyllaDB validation; it must not be reported as Cassandra-specific or universal.

overlap_review.messaging_reliability: No new instruction proposed: chat messages in a database are not equivalent to broker messages; effect/checkpoint/replay rules already exist.
overlap_review.microservice_data: Its data-ownership trigger should not expand to single-database capacity tuning.
overlap_review.new_skill_agent_category: Not proposed. User confirmation would be required before creating any new skill, agent or category.

not_adopted: Rust rewrites, ScyllaDB replacement, node counts or throughput as general recommendations
A one-endpoint-per-query data service as a required architecture
Consistent hashing as a complete solution to hot keys or a distributed exclusivity guarantee
Request coalescing as freshness, authorization, idempotency or durable exactly-once execution
Dual writes as atomic or sampled read equality as complete migration proof
Unconditional manual compaction, reduced tombstone retention or the historical storage topology as portable durability guidance
